finding.summary: Document clone persists target chunk tags, but copied index rows retain source tags (SQLite) or omit them (PostgreSQL); filtering by destination tag misses cloned content.

observed: New/reused destination tag returns 0 actual SQLite vector hits, expected 2 sources.
Best-effort tag creation failure leaves target chunk untagged but copied index TagID remains source tag.
Injected tag-update failures do not fire because no tag synchronization occurs; clone wrongly succeeds.

finding.fix: After CopyIndices succeeds and before CloneChunk succeeds, synchronize every persisted destination chunk TagID (including empty) through the composite index API. Propagate update failure into existing destination cleanup; clone is not marked complete.
test_design: Real temporary SQLite metadata/vector store with sqlite-vec and actual target-tag-filtered retrieval. Each chunk has body and generated-question rows.
New destination tag, reused tag, and unavailable mapping follow existing best-effort tag semantics; source rows unchanged.
SQLite triggers reject tag updates and optionally index deletion; verify failed state, successful cleanup or visibly retained references.
Normal executeKnowledgeClone retry removes failed clone, succeeds after outage, and repeated successful task delivery does not duplicate rows.
Existing image-vector copy fixture also asserts target tag map covers precisely copied chunk destinations.

root_review: All production diff and new SQLite integration tests read; tag remapping/rollback context traced; validation logs checked.
limitations: Actual sqlite-vec fixture tests target-tag retrieval. PostgreSQL/live vendor copy APIs not exercised by this group.
Copy completion now requires successful tag sync; visible failure follows existing cleanup and task retry.
Separate clone ContentRevision candidate remains under investigation; not covered by this fix.
